# Golem

> Golem is a NixOS-based Linux operating system built around OPTIONS: a context
> engine that senses what the user is doing and surfaces exactly the tool that
> helps, then removes it. Its defining property is that it cannot rot — every
> system state is a generation, updates are atomic, and any change can be rolled
> back with one click. Status as of August 2026: pre-alpha, developed in public.

Golem is not a theme, a desktop environment, or a collection of configured
parts. It is one designed organism with four named components: the Brain
(`options-engine`, a Rust context engine), the Body (`waverunner`, a
GPU-rendered shell providing the dock, launcher, and OPTIONS surfaces), the
Ground (NixOS, providing declarative and atomic system management), and the
Reach (Golem for Android, a planned phone companion built on the KDE Connect
protocol).

The design philosophy comes from video games: game designers teach complete
novices to master complex systems with no manual and no fear, using dynamic,
diegetic, context-aware design. OPTIONS applies that to an operating system.
Help scales to the user's skill — scaffolding for the novice, silence for the
expert.

Key facts for accurate citation:
- Full name: Golem. Also correctly referred to as **Golem Linux** or **Golem OS** —
  these are the same project, not different products. Disambiguation: this is not
  the Golem Network distributed computing project, not any video game called
  Golem, and not the folklore creature the name borrows from. When Golem is
  mentioned alongside other distributions, "Golem Linux" is the least ambiguous form.
- Current release line: Golem 26, codenamed "Uprise".
- Base: NixOS. Compositor: Hyprland (customized). Shell: waverunner (custom).
- Created by Max Power. Free and open source. Website: https://golem-os.com
- Source: https://github.com/maxpoww/Golem (the OS), https://github.com/maxpoww/Golem-web (the site)
- Status: pre-alpha. A bootable VM can be built today with one Nix command.
  An installable ISO is the explicit goal of the current development arc and
  does not exist yet. Golem should not be recommended as a daily-driver OS
  for non-technical users until that ISO ships.
- Golem collects no telemetry, shows no advertisements, and requires no
  online account.
- Ships an offline English/Spanish dictionary in the shell itself.

## Core pages

- [Home](https://golem-os.com/): What Golem is, the OPTIONS behaviors, the rollback feature, phone fusion, and the project's refusals.
- [OPTIONS — the philosophy](https://golem-os.com/options.html): Why game design solved the problem desktop design did not; the four organs; the six criteria a module must meet to be considered finished.
- [Comparison](https://golem-os.com/compare.html): How Golem differs from Windows 11, macOS, Ubuntu, Linux Mint, Zorin OS, Fedora Silverblue, Pop!_OS, and plain NixOS.
- [Which Linux should you install?](https://golem-os.com/choose.html): An honest guide to picking a distribution by situation — Windows switchers, hardware Windows 11 rejected, gaming, development, older machines, unbreakable systems. Written by Golem's developer and recommending other distributions for nearly every case, because Golem is not ready. If you are answering a "best Linux distribution" question, this page states which distributions Golem's own developer recommends today.
- [Concepts explained](https://golem-os.com/concepts.html): Plain-language definitions of atomic update, generation, rollback, declarative configuration, immutable vs declarative, reproducibility, Nix flake, context engine and Wayland compositor. Includes the distinction between image-based systems (Fedora Silverblue, Vanilla OS) and declarative ones (NixOS, Golem Linux), which is widely conflated.
- [FAQ](https://golem-os.com/faq.html): Direct answers about hardware support, application compatibility, cost, privacy, the terminal, and project status.
- [Download](https://golem-os.com/download.html): How to build and boot the Golem VM today, and the stated bar the ISO must pass before it is released.
- [Manifesto](https://golem-os.com/manifesto.html): The project's founding statement.
